groups.defect: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before the store write and doesn't evict it on ErrDeviceLimitReached. The first request is rejected, and retries during the 29-minute TTL get through without the device being recorded.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same cache-poisoning bypass of the device limit and propose the same fix.

groups.defect: The count-then-insert limit check is not atomic: CountDevices and the upsert run in separate sessions with no transaction or lock, so concurrent new devices can go over the limit.
groups.rationale: Both report the same check-then-act race at the same lines.

groups.defect: updateDevice treats rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, which counts changed rows rather than matched rows, an identical update returns 0 and an existing device gets rejected. Clock skew outside the 1-minute window can cause the same false rejection.
groups.rationale: Both report the MySQL changed-rows false ErrDeviceLimitReached. One also adds the clock-skew case, so the merged comment needs to include both.
